hl.w: One of the Marina Alta's most celebrated passes: switchbacks through orchard country from Parcent, with an optional extra climb to the old watchtower above the col (very steep last ramps).
The climb from Pego into the remote, almond-terraced Vall d'Ebo, one of the least-visited valleys.
A Vuelta pass, quieter and less photographed than Coll de Rates but just as hard on the legs.
Long, patient climb where professional teams have built winter fitness for decades.
Steady climb through cherry and almond groves with Aitana and Puigcampana ahead, and one of the region's best descents.
A proper mountain pass above Guadalest on the road to Alcoy.
Category-one Vuelta wall averaging over 11%, with ramps above 20%.
The climb over the shoulder of the Sierra de Bernia between Xaló and Benissa, best when the almonds blossom in February.

hl.n: Cumbre del Sol (Puig de la Llorença)
hl.w: A genuine climb from Benitatxell to the top of Puig de la Llorença, with a very nice view from the summit.
A proper climb on the quiet side of the Marina Alta interior.
A Vuelta pass (2023 and 2026), short and steep with ramps over 15%.

hl.n: Coll de la Font / El Miserat
hl.w: The second climb that turns the Vall d'Ebo ride into a full mountain circuit.
The highest paved point in the province, with some of the widest views on the coast (the last 6.6 km to the summit are normally closed to cyclists).
One of the four defining passes of the Aitana Tour.

hl.n: Port de la Llacuna and Balcón de Alicante
hl.w: The opening climb and the summit finish of the 2021 Vuelta stage.
The climb from the coast around Cala del Baladrar up to Fustera, with the Peñón de Ifach behind you.
A short climb from the rice fields of Pego toward el Ràfol d'Almúnia.
The limestone giant that appears early and guides you along the coast to Calp.
The limestone mountain that watches over Dénia and Xàbia.
The castle and reservoir at the top of the climb, or the start of the loop.

hl.n: Summit view from Puig de la Llorença
hl.w: A very nice view over the coast from the top of the Cumbre del Sol climb.
Cliffs, pine and turquoise water on the descent to the hidden cove.
Sea glimpses over rolling farmland, then the calm of Moraira harbour.

hl.n: Altea old town and blue-domed skyline
hl.w: The hilltop old town, crowned by its blue-domed church.

hl.n: Vall de Pop from the ridge road
hl.w: Vineyards and villages below the quiet ridge road between Pedreguer and Alcalalí (about 310 m).
The big mountains rising ahead or behind on the Benifallim and Tudons routes.

hl.n: View back over Dénia and over Jávea bay
hl.w: Dénia's harbour and castle behind you as the road climbs the shoulder of Montgó, then Jávea bay opening up below.
Views back to the sea from one of the coast's hill towns.
Beach terraces and promenades for the easy coastal rides.

hl.n: Vall de Gallinera, Valley of a Thousand Cherry Trees
hl.w: Eight villages on one quiet road; cherry blossom in late March and April.

hl.n: Pego marshes, rice fields and wetland birds
hl.w: Rice paddies, reed beds and herons: a side of Spain few visitors see.

hl.n: Xaló valley vineyards and almond terraces
hl.w: Vineyards on one side, almond and olive terraces on the other; almond blossom in February.
Citrus country scenting the air along quiet farm roads.
An old railway line turned quiet green path, with no traffic.

hl.n: Pine forest and almond terraces of Castell de Castells
hl.w: A village apart from time, ringed by pine and almond.
Orchard-lined lanes inland of Pedreguer.

hl.n: Cherry and almond groves of Benifallim
hl.w: Blossom-and-fruit terraces on the Benifallim climbs.

hl.n: Loquat orchards of Callosa d'en Sarrià
hl.w: Terraces of loquat (níspero) trees, often under white netting; the fruit ripens in spring.
Waterfalls and turquoise pools on the river Algar, a short detour from Callosa d'en Sarrià.
A lagoon in the middle of Calp where flamingos often feed.
Tracing the river through Benimeli, Beniarbeig, Pedreguer and El Verger.
The 'Eagle's Nest': castle village on a rock above the reservoir.
Alcalalí, Benigembla, Murla, Llíber and Xaló: quiet villages with church bells.
The village wine cooperative, with tastings of local muscatel and red wines.
Wine tasting with dinner at Bodega Montesanco in Teulada, where the Syncrosfera to Montesanco rides finish.
Wicker and esparto worked by hand for generations, and Spanish guitars still made; workshops to browse.
Narrow streets and a cathedral-sized church; lunch and coffee in the old square.
Cobbled old town leading to the seafront.
A remote mountain village, a real discovery.
Xixona is famous for turrón; Alcoy's mountains shaped generations of local climbers.
The castle on the hill above Dénia's harbour, looking out over the town and the sea.
The Gothic church of Sant Bartomeu, built like a fortress, in the heart of the old town.
A medieval defensive tower in the village square of Alcalalí.
Arcaded farm buildings where muscatel grapes were dried into raisins, typical of the Marina Alta countryside.
The Font dels Xorrets in Polop's old town.
Cycling bar in Xaló (Carrer Església 14): coffee, crêpes, tortilla, bike shop and mechanic. Closed Sunday and Monday.
Small cyclists' café on Plaça Mosquera 2, popular before and after Coll de Rates: coffee and homemade cake. Closed weekends.
Bike rental at Av de la Sénia 14, Alcalalí, opening its own cyclists' café (expected late November / December 2026); delivers bikes to hotels.
The classic stop at the top of Coll de Rates: terrace with views over the Xaló valley to the sea; apple strudel and hot chocolate are favourites. Closed Monday.

hl.n: Blanca Bikes Base Camp Café, Parcent
hl.w: Café and bike rental at the foot of Coll de Rates (Av de Dénia 15, Parcent), with views of the climb. Open daily.

favorites.title: Mirava favorites from our hotels
favorites.lede: The rides we use in our Bikes & Bites programs, starting at the hotel door.

items.text: The gentle way to start: round Montgó from the hotel door, through the orange groves of Jesús Pobre, along Dénia's coast and back across Xàbia's countryside. Our favorite first ride, for settling into the bike.

Inland on quiet lanes through Pedreguer and the sleepy valley village of Sagra, past Orba's orchards to Alcalalí and Musette Café at the foot of Coll de Rates. Home over the ridge road at about 310 m, with the Vall de Pop below.
Over Monte Pego and down to Pego's rice fields and marshes, where herons lift off the paddies, then back through Orba's orchards. Short climbs, long views and almost no traffic.

items.end: Ends in Calp, at the lunch stop
items.text: One way, with lunch at the end: over the ridge road to Llíber, Senija and hilltop Benissa, then the long descent through Fustera with the Peñón de Ifach growing ahead. Finish by Calp's salt lake, where flamingos often feed.

A full coastal day: round Montgó to Xàbia, up the stiff climb to the top of Puig de la Llorença above Cumbre del Sol, along the coast past Moraira and up through Fustera. Lunch at L'Espigó in Benissa's old town after about 50 km.
The same coastal climbs with a longer road to lunch: from Benissa on to Xaló and Bistro Selene after about 57 km, then home through Gata de Gorgos.

The two-valley classic from the hotel door: over Monte Pego into the Vall de Gallinera, the Valley of a Thousand Cherry Trees, across to the Vall d'Ebo and down to Pego's rice fields. Best in late March and April, when the cherries blossom.
Down the coast to Dénia, round Montgó to Xàbia and back inland through the orange groves of La Xara. Gentle climbing and plenty of coffee stops by the sea.
Over Monte Pego above the rice fields, through Pedreguer, round Montgó to Xàbia and home along the coast through Dénia.

favorites.note: From Marriott La Sella, the Las Marinas, Montgó Loop, Coll de Rates and Sierra de Bernia routes above all start at the door.
